label: At GO in the last ten trials, ramps up with trial number after an unrewarded a2-to-S2 trial.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 90, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec == 9) * (prev_reward == 1)
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 90, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * (ep_dec == 9) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 90, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 90, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec == 9) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 90, 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec == 9) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * (ep_trial >= 98)
explanation: Fires only at GO in episode trials 90-99. Its magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a2 -> S2 unrewarded (common, no reward), and grows roughly linearly with ep_trial past 90 (about +0.17 per trial, reaching ~1.5-1.7 by trial 97-99). After a rewarded previous trial it is essentially silent (the second term cancels the late-GO timing baseline). Other unrewarded patterns (a1 S2 u, S1 unrewarded) add little; belief_lo, the trial before, and choice/state contribute nothing measurable. The 8-term free fit (dev 0.777) adds only a small saturation at trials 98-99 and minor corrections over the 2-term short form (dev 0.763). Only observed variables are used.

issues: Minor: the ramp is not quite linear. Fitting one weight per trial for a2 S2 u at GO gives 0.04 (t90), 0.13, 0.29, 0.49, 0.71, 0.95, 1.09, 1.24, 1.32 and 1.43 (t99). It rises by about 0.2 per trial early on and flattens after t96. The explanation's '+0.17 per trial' is the fitted average, so it holds.

The worst-fit windows are mostly at window starts, where the previous trial is unknown ('?') but the shown reward is r0. The feature fires there at 1.3-1.6 and the model predicts about 0.1. This is a gap in the data, not in the interpretation. After a1 S2 u the feature sometimes fires at about 1.0-1.2, but the systematic residual for that pattern is only +0.002. Adding an a1 S2 u ramp term raises test R^2 only from 0.748 to 0.752.

Pooling all S2-unrewarded trials ((prev_state==S2)*(prev_reward==0)*ramp) drops test R^2 to 0.54, and pooling all unrewarded trials drops it to 0.23. So the claim that the effect is specific to a2 S2 u checks out.

Removing the second term (prev_reward==1 at GO in the last decile) drops test R^2 to 0.695, so that term does real work: it cancels the timing baseline. A step at trial >= 97 instead of the ramp gives only 0.44, so the ramp is real.

Adding belief_lo, a reward two trials back (tv('reward',-2)), or an extra decile-9 step for a2 S2 u each adds less than 0.001 test R^2. That confirms the 'adds nothing' claims. No systematic error remains by phase or previous-trial pattern: all cells have mean error at or below 0.011 in absolute value.
